ex: We bought a domain for our new website.
The domain name costs ten dollars a year.
Can you check if this domain is still free?
He owns several domains for his small business.
domain.note: Most often "domain" means an area of work or knowledge: "Cooking is her domain."

leukemia.note: Uncountable: leukemia (not "a leukemia"). British spelling: leukaemia.

ex: Neon lights glowed above the bar all night.
Neon is a gas used in bright signs.
The sign over the shop is pink neon.
The old neon sign outside the cafe is broken.
neon.note: Uncountable (not "a neon"). Also used for very bright colors: neon green.

ex: She baked chocolate brownies for the party.
I'd like a brownie with ice cream, please.
These brownies are soft in the middle.
Cut the brownies into small squares before serving.
I need a strong espresso after lunch.
She ordered a double espresso at the cafe.
This machine makes very good espresso.
He drinks three espressos a day at work.
Mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
The letter mu often means "micro" in science.
In this formula, mu stands for the average.
Can you show me how to type mu on my phone?
Cows produce a lot of methane every day.
Methane is a strong greenhouse gas.
The gas for our stove is mostly methane.
The leak released methane into the air.
methane.note: Uncountable: methane, a lot of methane (not "a methane").

nickel.note: The metal is uncountable. In the US, "a nickel" is also a 5-cent coin: "Do you have a nickel?"

primaries.note: Plural of "primary"; one election is a "primary."

ex: A grizzly crossed the road in front of our car.
The grizzly caught a fish in the river.
Grizzlies live in the mountains of Alaska and Canada.
If you see a grizzly, never run away.
I added some kale to my smoothie.
Kale is a healthy green vegetable.
She made a kale salad for lunch today.
Cook the kale with a little garlic and oil.
kale.note: Uncountable: some kale, a lot of kale (not "a kale").

establishment.note: Most often it means starting something or a business place: "the establishment of a new school."

ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
They washed the exterior of the car on Sunday.
The building has a modern glass exterior.
The exterior of our school needs new paint.
exterior.note: Also an adjective: exterior walls, an exterior door.

ex: The ship hit an iceberg and sank.
Most of an iceberg is under the water.
We saw huge icebergs near the coast of Greenland.
Ships must watch out for icebergs in the north.
She plays folk on her guitar every evening.
I prefer folk to pop music.
The festival has folk, jazz, and blues bands.
Do you listen to folk, or do you prefer rock?
folk.note: Most often "folk" means people: "country folk." "Folks" is informal for people or parents.

ex: We flew to Turkey on a cheap charter.
Our charter leaves at six in the morning.
Charter flights are often cheaper than regular ones.
They booked a boat charter for the whole day.
charter.note: Most often "charter" is an official document of rights or rules: "a city charter."

ex: Old songs fill me with nostalgia.
He felt nostalgia for his school days.
The movie is full of eighties nostalgia.
Looking at old photos gives me a feeling of nostalgia.
nostalgia.note: Uncountable: "a feeling of nostalgia", not "a nostalgia".

protagonist.note: Formal; "main character" is more common in speech.

ex: Please eat your broccoli because it is good for you.
I steamed some broccoli for dinner.
Broccoli is a green vegetable with a lot of vitamins.
Can you add some broccoli to the pasta?
"Meow," said the kitten when it wanted food.
The cat says meow when it is hungry.
My little son says "meow" every time he sees a cat.
Meow! Our cat is waiting by the door again.
meow.note: Also a noun and a verb: "The cat gave a loud meow." British spelling: miaow.

ex: My grandpa is a boomer, born in 1955.
Many boomers are retiring from work now.
Boomers grew up after the Second World War.
Is your grandmother a boomer or older?
boomer.note: Informal, short for "baby boomer"; can sound rude ("OK, boomer").

ex: Put the car in reverse to leave the parking space.
The car is stuck in reverse and won't go forward.
She shifted into reverse to park near the store.
The back of a coin is called the reverse.
reverse.note: Most often "reverse" is a verb or adjective: "reverse a decision", "in reverse order".

ex: The referee gave a penalty in the last minute.
He scored the winning penalty for his team.
Our goalkeeper saved the penalty and the fans cheered.
The game ended in a penalty shootout.
penalty.note: Most often "penalty" means a punishment or fine: "a penalty for late payment."

starter.note: Often "starter" means a player who starts a game, or (UK) the first course of a meal.

ex: He was a famous flying ace in the war.
She is an ace at math and helps her friends.
My brother is an ace with computers.
Ask our neighbor; he is an ace at fixing cars.
ace.note: Most often an "ace" is a playing card: "the ace of hearts." To "ace a test" means to do very well.

ex: Fascism spread across Europe in the 1930s.
Millions of people died fighting fascism in the war.
This book explains the rise of fascism in Italy.
Fascism is the opposite of democracy.
A proton has a positive electric charge.
A hydrogen atom has just one proton.
Protons are found in the center of an atom.
The number of protons tells you the element.
This shampoo is good for a dry scalp.
She has a dry, itchy scalp in winter.
Massage your scalp gently when you wash your hair.
Wear a hat to protect your scalp from the sun.
I put avocado on my toast every morning.
This avocado is not ripe yet.
Cut the avocado in half and remove the seed.
Avocados are rich in healthy fats.

discourse.note: Formal, mostly uncountable; in daily speech use "discussion" or "debate".

ex: He is a football fanatic who watches every game.
She is a fitness fanatic and runs every day.
My brother is a fanatic about clean cars.
Religious fanatics attacked the small town.

cider.note: In the US, "cider" often means non-alcoholic juice; alcoholic is "hard cider".

ex: Patience is an important attribute for a teacher.
Honesty is his best attribute as a manager.
What attributes make a good leader?
Each file has attributes like size and date.
attribute.note: Often "attribute" is a verb (stress on -TRIB-): "She attributes her success to hard work."

ex: This photo has very strong contrast.
Turn up the contrast on your screen, please.
There is a big contrast between city and village life.
I like the contrast between the black and white walls.
He wore a gray hoodie and jeans.
Put on your hoodie because it's cold outside.
She bought a hoodie with the school logo.
My favorite hoodie has a big front pocket.
